title: VPC BGP & MTU preflight + Terraform quirks checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft checklist + troubleshooting notes focused on the intersection of BGP/MTU/routing preflight validation and Terraform idempotency quirks we keep hitting during private (VPC/on-prem) installs and upgrades. Goal is a short set of fast smoke probes first-responder on customer installs and a handful of tf workarounds we can add to the modules or hand to SREs during escalations.

Context / when to use:
- Run this before the first bootstrap on a VPC or on-prem cluster (especially multi-rack or multi-topo networks).
- Run after network topology changes and before agent bootstrap during upgrade windows.
- Use as a troubleshooting checklist when customers see high packet loss, asymmetric routing, or perf regressions post-upgrade.

Quick summary checklist (5-minute triage):
- Confirm MTU consistent across path: run mtu probe from at least two hosts to each peer device. Expected: no ICMP fragmentation messages; path MTU == configured MTU.
- Verify BGP adjacency: show BGP summary on both sides, ensure prefixes learned and proper AS path.
- Validate ECMP behavior: traceroute with large flow ids to detect hashing asymmetry.
- Check management plane DNS/NTP reachability: curl to control plane endpoints and query NTP server offsets.
- Confirm TF state sanity: terraform plan shows no diff for network resources after provisioning. If diffs appear, capture plan and related resource diffs.

Detailed probes and commands (copy-paste friendly):
1) MTU / path MTU probes
- ping -M do -s 1432 <peer-ip>  # for 1500 MTU, reduce payload until success
- iperf3 -c <peer> -M 1428 -P 4 -t 10  # look for retransmits and throughput drop
- Expected notes: consistent MTU across switch layers; fragmentation or ICMP frag-needed indicates misconfigured tunnel or load balancer with lower MTU.

2) BGP adjacency and prefix checks
- On leaf/router: vtysh -c 'show ip bgp summary' OR show bgp ipv4 unicast summary
- Validate: state = ESTABLISHED, neighbor uptime reasonable, prefixes in, no flap storms
- If adjacency missing: check TTL, auth keys, ACLs, and whether TCP MSS or PMTU causes session to fail.

3) Asymmetric routing / ECMP debugging
- traceroute -T -p 5201 <peer>  # TCP traceroute, compare ports/hops from different hosts
- tcptraceroute or mtr with flowhash knobs to detect path asymmetry
- Quick test: run curl multiple times with --resolve to force same 5-tuple; if responses come from different backends with spikes, suspect ECMP hash mismatch or NAT session stickiness.

4) Control plane checks (DNS / NTP / KMS endpoints)
- dig +short @<dns> redwood-control.example.com -> expect internal IPs resolvable from hosts
- chronyc tracking OR ntpq -p  # NTP offset should be <100ms for stable token expiry
- curl -v https://control-plane.example.internal/health -> TLS handshake success, 200 OK

5) Terraform-specific sanity probes (post-apply):
- terraform plan -var-file=... (after apply) -> should be empty diff for network and route resources.
- Common flaky resources: bgp_peer, route_table associations, cloud provider-managed MTU values (some providers return 0 or default). Capture plan JSON when not empty: terraform show -json > plan.json

Known TF quirks and mitigations (short):
- Quirk: provider returns computed MTU (0) vs desired field. Mitigation: add lifecycle ignore_changes for mtus that provider overrides and create a post-provision verify job that fixes devices via provider CLI if needed.
- Quirk: BGP ASN or neighbor config occasionally reordered by provider API leading to diff churn. Mitigation: normalize lists in module (sort by neighbor IP) and use schema validation to block malformed ASNs.
- Quirk: Route table ephemeral IDs change on upgrades causing association replace. Mitigation: pin dependency ordering with explicit depends_on for critical associations; add a small sleep/retry in apply automation for eventual-consistent APIs.

Upgrade window specific checklist (pre-upgrade -> during -> post-upgrade):
Pre-upgrade (2–24 hours before):
- Snapshot TF state and store in artifact store (terraform state pull + zip).
- Run connectivity smoke: ping hub + all control IPs, BGP adjacency check, mtp/iperf samples saved.
- Take a quick traceroute matrix from each AZ to others and save.
- Ensure rollback plan documented: which module commit to revert to and where statefile snapshot is.

During upgrade (fast checks to stop and rollback):
- Monitor BGP session count and prefix delta every 30s (automated alert).
- If loss >5% across control channels for >60s or BGP session drop, pause upgrade.
- If terraform plan unexpectedly modifies core route resources, auto-pause and open a safety PR for manual review.

Post-upgrade quick smoke (0–15 minutes after):
- Confirm BGP neighbors stable and prefixes fully converged.
- Run a short iperf burst (30s) across key flows and confirm throughput within 10% of baseline.
- Run tokenized end-to-end test that exercises control plane registration and a model load request to verify data path.

Troubleshooting patterns we see (field notes):
- Symptom: intermittent large token latencies right after upgrade. Pattern: MTU mismatch on a new tunnel introduced by upgraded cloud router image. Fix: roll back router image or adjust MTU on tunnel endpoints.
- Symptom: terraform applies keep toggling a BGP neighbor local_as field. Pattern: provider API returns int vs string mismatch. Fix: coerce to string in module variable validation and add an acceptance test.
- Symptom: one leaf flaps BGP whenever large model pulls happen. Pattern: port-channel hashing causing TCP streams split; fix by pinning sessions to an active path via source port normalization on load balancer or adjust flowhash algorithm on switch.

Customer-facing quick 'what we ask you to run' bundle (one script to run and paste output into ticket):
- ./collect-network-preflight.sh <target-controller-ip> --includes mtuprobes,bgp-summary,iperf,mtr,dns,ntp
- Script should produce a tar.gz with: mtuprobes.log, bgp-summary.txt, iperf.log, traceroutes/*, tf-plan.json, terraform-show.json

Notes for TF module maintainers (action items):
- Add deterministic sorting hooks for neighbor lists and route rules (PR open referenced above).
- Add an acceptance test that runs on a small ephemeral environment to exercise BGP neighbor churn and MTU variation.
- Add a post-apply verification step (lightweight) that runs the mtuprobes and fixes obvious mismatches using provider APIs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize a min MTU of 9000 for all internal tunnels or allow mixed MTU with auto-fragmentation? (impact: increases operator complexity vs reduces per-packet overhead)
- Do we keep lifecycle ignore_changes for MTU as a longterm pattern or invest in provider work to normalize?

References / links (quick):
- Internal git PR: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/58
- Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/98765/VPC+Preflight+Runbook
- JIRA: INF-4021 (bgp-mtu-preflight-automation)

Notes to self at end: keep this doc short — most responders want checklist + 1 paste-friendly script + 3 troubleshooting rules. Next pass: add sample outputs for expected BGP summary and sample plan.json snippet to speed up Triage.

-- Priya (draft)
